setup.zh: 树比外面高一倍，树皮黑得像铁。你们循着蹄印追到山涧边，蹄印比你的巴掌还宽。
setup.en: The trees are twice as tall as outside, bark black as iron. You follow the tracks to a stream; they are wider than your palm.

recap.zh: 黑松岭深处，你们找到了一头大鹿的蹄印；你每一百步刻一道记号。林子深处，一只山鹧鸪叫了三声，像人在喊「……回来……」。
recap.en: Deep in Black Pine Ridge you found a big deer's hoofprints; every hundred paces you cut a mark. Deep in the trees a mountain partridge called three times, like a voice crying "…Come back…"

zh: 松针厚如毯，踩下去无声。
山涧边，一行蹄印，比巴掌还宽。
en: Trees twice as tall, bark like iron.
Needles thick as a rug; no footstep sounds.
By the stream, hoofprints wider than a palm.

text.zh: 印子边上的泥还湿着，涧水正一丝丝渗进去——鹿过去，还不到一个时辰。
text.en: The mud at the print's edge is still wet, the stream seeping in thread by thread: the deer passed less than a watch ago.

text.zh: 蹄印到涧边一块青石前便断了；石上青苔刮掉两道，石头那边的软泥里，又是半个蹄印。
text.en: The prints stop at a grey stone by the stream. Two strips of moss are scraped off it, and in the soft mud beyond lies half a print.

text.zh: 涧边的枯草尖上挂着几根鹿毛，灰褐色，粗得像马鬃——好大一头鹿。
text.en: A few deer hairs hang on the dry grass by the stream, grey-brown and coarse as a horse's mane. A very big deer.

look_hint.zh: 蹄印在涧边断了。鹿总不会飞——你爹蹲在那儿不作声，等你看出个名堂来。
look_hint.en: The prints break off at the stream. A deer cannot fly — your father crouches there in silence, waiting for you to make it out.

story.zh:
黑松岭的树比外面的高一倍，树皮是黑的，摸上去凉冰冰的，像摸着一块铁；脚下的松针厚得像毯子，一脚踩下去，半点声息也无。他爹走在前面，这许多年来，头一回走得比儿子还轻。

晌午过后，蹄印引着两人到了一处山涧边，在涧边的软泥里踩得又深又清楚。是一头大的，蹄印比小满的巴掌还宽，前山十年都没见过这么大的鹿。小满先看风——涧边的芦草尖儿齐齐往他们这边歪，风是从鹿那头吹过来的，它闻不着他们。

他爹瞧了一眼草尖，又瞧了儿子一眼，没有说话，小满却觉得他夸了自己一句。

他爹蹲在地下，摸着那个蹄印，手在发颤，低声道：「一张鹿皮……够交马家的租。剩下的肉，给你娘换一身新棉袄。给吴婆婆，送一条腿。再给阿禾家……赔一颗白菜。」说着抬起头来，冲小满笑了一下。自打马三走后，这是小满头一回见他笑。

一头鹿，他分了四份，一份也没给他自己。
story.en:
The trees of Black Pine Ridge stood twice as tall as those outside; their bark was black and icy to the touch, like touching a slab of iron; underfoot the needles lay thick as a rug, and a footfall made no sound at all. His father went ahead, and for the first time in many years walked more lightly than his son.

After noon the hoofprints led the two of them to a mountain stream, pressed deep and clear in the soft mud of the bank. A big one, prints wider than Xiaoman's palm; the front hills hadn't seen a deer that size in ten years. Xiaoman read the wind first — the reed tips along the stream all leaned their way; the wind blew from the deer toward them, so it couldn't smell them.

His father glanced at the reed tips, then at his son, and said nothing, yet Xiaoman felt he'd been praised.

His father crouched and felt the hoofprint, his hand trembling, and said low: "One deer hide… that covers the Mas' rent. The meat that's left, a new padded coat for your mother. A leg for Granny Wu. And for Ahe's family… a cabbage to make good." He looked up and gave Xiaoman a smile. It was the first time Xiaoman had seen him smile since Ma San left.

One deer, and he'd split it four ways, and not one share for himself.

label.en: Follow the prints, a mark every hundred paces

exits.means: follows the deer tracks, cuts a mark every hundred paces, keeps the rules

story.zh:
蹄印往黑松岭的更深处去。两人又追了一个时辰，从断碑数起，小满一路刻了四十一道记号，刻得手指头都麻了。这一个时辰里，有两件事，他当时没有跟他爹说，后来也没有跟他娘说。

头一件是记号。刻到第二十几道的时候，他回头望了一眼，只见来路上那一溜树干上的刀口白生生的，一道一道排过去——排得不对。他刻记号是有规矩的，一律刻在树干朝着来路的那一面，好叫回来的人一眼便看得见。

可这一眼望过去，倒有两三道刻在了树的背面，冲着林子里头，是刻给别的什么人看的。

他心里一跳，折回去十几步细看，那几道记号却好端端地刻在朝来路的那一面，刀口新鲜，树脂还在一丝一丝地往外渗。他站在那里看了半天，终于决定：是自己眼花了。饿的人眼花，这是常理。

可他再往前刻下一道的时候，「笃」的一声，过了一会儿，林子深处也「笃」的一声，隔得很远，慢了半拍，仿佛前头还有一个人，也在树上刻记号。他停了手，那边也停了。

他站着听了片刻，心想，是回声——只是他在蒙山爬了十二年的树，从没听见过哪一处的回声，是从前头传过来的。

第二件是鸟。林子深处，忽然从头顶上不知什么地方，传来一声长长的鸟啼，拖着一个尾音，又细又远，听在耳朵里，竟像是有个人在很远很远的地方，一声一声地喊：「……回来……」他爹登时站住了。

那一双听得见三里外獐子踩断枯枝的耳朵，这一回偏着头，听了很久。那声音叫了三声，便不叫了。他爹的脸色有点发白，过了好一会儿，才道：「山鹧鸪。叫起来像人。山里有东西喊你，别应。」说完便低下头去，接着看那蹄印，再没有提起。

小满心里却忍不住想：要真是有人在喊，喊的是谁？这林子里头，除了他和他爹，还有谁该回来？这念头一冒出来，他便不敢往下想了，把它和那几道看错了的记号搁在一处，压在心底，压得严严实实。

他把这两件事在心里算了一算：记号是眼花，「笃」是回声，鸟是山鹧鸪。几件事都有了着落，都算不得「不对劲」，第三条规矩，用不着。可他把刀攥得更紧了。
story.en:
The hoofprints led deeper into Black Pine Ridge. They followed for another hour, and counting from the stele Xiaoman cut forty-one marks along the way, till his fingers went numb. In that hour two things happened that he didn't tell his father at the time, nor his mother later.

The first was the marks. Somewhere past the twentieth he looked back: the knife-cuts on the trunks behind them showed white, one after another — and they were wrong. He had a rule for marks: always on the side of the trunk facing the way they'd come, so whoever came back would see them at a glance.

Yet looking back now, two or three had been cut on the far side of the tree, facing into the forest, cut for someone else to read.

His heart jumped; he went back a dozen paces for a closer look, but the marks were all cut neatly on the side facing the way back, fresh, the resin still oozing out thread by thread. He stood there looking a long while and finally decided his eyes had played a trick.

A hungry man's eyes play tricks; that stood to reason. But as he cut the next one — *tock* — after a moment, deep in the woods, there came another *tock*, far off, half a beat late, as if someone ahead were also cutting marks in trees. He stopped; so did the other.

He stood listening a moment and told himself it was an echo — only, in twelve years of climbing trees on Mount Meng, he'd never heard an echo that came from ahead.

The second thing was the bird. Deep in the woods, from somewhere overhead, there came a long birdcall trailing off, thin and far, and to the ear it was for all the world like someone very, very far away calling, again and again: "…Come back…" His father stopped dead.

Those ears that could hear a river deer snap a twig three li away tilted and listened for a long time. It called three times and fell silent. His father had gone a little pale, and only after a good while said, "Mountain partridge. Sounds like a person. If something in the mountains calls you, don't answer." Then he bent to the hoofprints again and never mentioned it.

But Xiaoman couldn't help wondering: if it really was someone calling, whom were they calling? In these woods, besides him and his father, who else was due to come back? The moment the thought came up he didn't dare follow it; he put it with the marks he'd misread and pressed them down deep, very firmly.

He did the sums on the two things: the marks were his eyes, the *tock* was an echo, the bird was a partridge. Each had its explanation; none counted as "something wrong"; rule three wasn't needed. But he gripped the knife tighter.

refuse.zh: 蹄印到涧边就断了，往哪儿追？先看清楚。
refuse.en: The prints stop at the stream. Follow them where? Look first.
